**A complex model only helps if its flexibility matches useful structure in the data.** Some forecasting benchmarks are dominated by trend and seasonality that a linear mapping captures well. A large attention model can overfit, optimize poorly, or fail to exploit temporal order effectively, allowing a carefully evaluated linear baseline to win. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

That result challenges a particular architecture and evaluation setup, not the possibility of transformer forecasting. Always compare against seasonal-naive and linear methods before attributing gains to model size.

**Patches change the unit of representation.** Instead of treating every scalar timestamp as a separate token, a patch groups a short local window. The model sees local shape within the patch and attends across fewer tokens. For a length-1024 sequence split into nonoverlapping patches of 16, attention sees 64 patch tokens rather than 1024 individual positions, though the full architecture adds other costs.

Foundation models add broad pretraining and different normalization, tokenization, and forecasting objectives. PatchTST, Chronos, TimesFM, and Moirai are not interchangeable implementations of one method. Compare horizons, covariate availability, tuning budgets, and pretraining overlap. Better tokenization does not eliminate regime shifts or unavailable future inputs. Evaluate the forecasts the application will actually consume using leak-free rolling splits.

**Technical details and references.**

Simple linear baselines can excel when benchmarks are dominated by stable trend/seasonality and complex models fail to exploit temporal ordering or are poorly tuned. This is evidence about benchmark/model configurations, not proof that transformers cannot forecast. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

Patch-based models encode short windows rather than individual scalar timestamps, exposing local patterns and reducing attention token count. Foundation models add broad pretraining and normalization/tokenization choices; Chronos, TimesFM, and Moirai do not share one identical architecture or objective.

Compare with seasonal naive, linear, and statistical baselines using leak-free rolling evaluation, matched horizons, covariates, and tuning budgets. Check cross-dataset pretraining overlap. Improved tokenization alone does not solve regime shift, missing future covariates, or the mismatch between point-error metrics and business decisions.
